title: Forming adverbs; comparative and superlative (mieux, le mieux)
spec: Adverbs: comparative and superlative: regular, including mieux, le mieux
summary: Most adverbs are the feminine adjective + -ment: lent → lente → lentement; heureux → heureuse → heureusement.
If the masculine adjective ends in a vowel, add -ment to the masculine: vrai → vraiment, poli → poliment, facile → facilement.
Adjectives in -ant change to -amment and those in -ent to -emment (both said 'amment'): courant → couramment, évident → évidemment.
Learn the irregular ones: bon → bien, mauvais → mal, rapide → vite (or rapidement), gentil → gentiment.
Comparative: plus / moins / aussi + adverb + que: Il court plus vite que moi.
Superlative: le plus / le moins + adverb, always with le: C'est Léa qui nage le plus vite.
bien → mieux (better) → le mieux (best): Je chante mieux que mon frère.
meilleur is the adjective (with a noun, agrees); mieux is the adverb (with a verb, never changes): une meilleure note, elle joue mieux.

cards.front: How are most French adverbs formed from adjectives?
cards.back: Take the feminine form of the adjective and add -ment: lent → lente → lentement (slowly); doux → douce → doucement (gently); heureux → heureuse → heureusement (luckily).

cards.why: Feminine adjective lente + -ment gives the adverb lentement.
The feminine of heureux is heureuse; add -ment: heureusement.

cards.front: When do you add -ment to the masculine adjective instead of the feminine?
cards.back: When the masculine adjective already ends in a vowel: vrai → vraiment, poli → poliment, absolu → absolument, facile → facilement, rapide → rapidement.

cards.prompt: Après le match, je suis ___ fatigué.
cards.en: After the match, I'm really tired.
cards.why: vrai ends in a vowel, so -ment is added straight to the masculine: vraiment.

cards.front: How do adjectives ending in -ant and -ent form their adverbs?
cards.back: -ant → -amment and -ent → -emment, both pronounced 'amment': courant → couramment, évident → évidemment, récent → récemment, patient → patiemment. Watch out: lent → lentement.

cards.why: Adjectives ending in -ant form their adverb with -amment: courant → couramment.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with one adverb.
cards.why: patient ends in -ent, so the adverb ends in -emment: patiemment.

cards.front: What are the adverbs from bon, mauvais and rapide?
cards.back: bon → bien (well), mauvais → mal (badly), rapide → vite or rapidement (quickly). Also gentil → gentiment (kindly).

cards.prompt: Hier soir, j'ai ___ dormi à cause du bruit.
cards.en: Last night I slept badly because of the noise.
cards.why: The adverb from mauvais is irregular: mal. Short adverbs go between avoir and the past participle.

cards.front: How do you compare adverbs, and which article does the superlative use?
cards.back: plus / moins / aussi + adverb + que: Il conduit plus lentement que moi. Superlative: le plus / le moins + adverb, always le, whatever the subject: Ma sœur court le plus vite.

cards.prompt: Mon père conduit ___ que ma mère.
cards.en: My father drives more carefully than my mother.
cards.why: Comparative of an adverb: plus + adverb + que; prudent → prudemment (-ent → -emment).

cards.en: Léa runs the fastest in the whole team.
cards.why: Superlative of an adverb: le plus + adverb. It is always le, even with a female subject.

cards.en: My mate swims as well as me.
cards.why: Comparison of equality: aussi + adverb + que. bien itself does not change here.

cards.front: meilleur or mieux: how do you choose?
cards.back: meilleur is an adjective: it describes a noun and agrees (un meilleur film, une meilleure note). mieux is an adverb: it describes a verb and never changes (elle chante mieux). bien → mieux → le mieux.

cards.prompt: Depuis mon séjour en France, je parle ___ qu'avant.
cards.en: Since my stay in France, I speak better than before.
cards.why: 'Better' describes the verb parler, so use the adverb mieux (never plus bien).

cards.prompt: Dans ma famille, c'est ma mère qui cuisine ___.
cards.en: In my family, it's my mother who cooks the best.
cards.why: The superlative of the adverb bien is le mieux; it stays le even though the subject is feminine.

cards.prompt: Ma sœur a eu une ___ note que moi en maths.
cards.en: My sister got a better mark than me in maths.
cards.why: 'Better' describes the noun note, so use the adjective meilleur, which agrees with the feminine noun: meilleure.

cards.prompt: Cette année, je fais du sport ___ que l'année dernière.
cards.en: This year I do sport less regularly than last year.
cards.why: Comparative of inferiority: moins + adverb + que. régulier → feminine régulière → régulièrement (keep the grave accent).
